answer.worked:
The angle is in quadrant II, with reference angle $\pi-\frac{2\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{3}$. Sine is positive.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}&=\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\\\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{align*}$$

The angle is in quadrant III, with reference angle $\frac{7\pi}{6}-\pi=\frac{\pi}{6}$. Tangent is positive.

answer.worked:
Quadrant II; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Sine is positive.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}&=\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant II; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Cosine is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}&=-\cos\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=-\frac12\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant II; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Cosine is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\frac{5\pi}{6}&=-\cos\frac{\pi}{6}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant III; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Tangent is positive.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{4\pi}{3}&=\tan\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=\sqrt3\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant II; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$. Tangent is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}&=-\tan\frac{\pi}{4}\\&=-1\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant IV; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Cosine is positive.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}&=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=\frac12\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant III; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$. Sine is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}&=-\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\\&=-\frac1{\sqrt2}\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant III; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Tangent is positive.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{7\pi}{6}&=\tan\frac{\pi}{6}\\&=\frac1{\sqrt3}\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant II; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$. Cosine is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\frac{3\pi}{4}&=-\cos\frac{\pi}{4}\\&=-\frac1{\sqrt2}\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant II; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Sine is positive.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}&=\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\\&=\frac12\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant IV; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$. Tangent is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{7\pi}{4}&=-\tan\frac{\pi}{4}\\&=-1\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant III; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Cosine is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}&=-\cos\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=-\frac12\end{aligned}$$

Quadrant IV; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Sine is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}&=-\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{13\pi}{6}-2\pi&=\frac{\pi}{6}\end{aligned}$$
The terminal side is in quadrant I, where cosine is positive.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos\frac{13\pi}{6}&=\cos\frac{\pi}{6}\\&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{11\pi}{3}-2\pi&=\frac{5\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$$
Quadrant IV; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Tangent is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{11\pi}{3}&=-\tan\frac{\pi}{3}\\&=-\sqrt3\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{23\pi}{6}-2\pi&=\frac{11\pi}{6}\end{aligned}$$
Quadrant IV; reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Sine is negative.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin\frac{23\pi}{6}&=-\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\\&=-\frac12\end{aligned}$$

Two sectors are constructed along a straight line $AOC$.

The first sector has radius $4$ m and second sector has radius $3$ m, as shown below.
